name: zork
desc: Dungeon modified from FORTRAN to C
why: A faithful C port of the 1970s text adventure that started it all, a piece of computing history you can actually play.

brief.what_it_is: Dungeon, also called Zork, is a text adventure game whose source code is in the public domain. The repository holds a C version of the mainframe game, converted from the FORTRAN source of Zork 2.6. You type commands at a prompt and the game replies with text describing the world. The README's startup banner, which appears in the fetched page, reads: "Welcome to Dungeon. This version created 11-MAR-91." It then shows the opening scene, a field west of a white house with a boarded front door.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project's primary design goal is code preservation. It aims to keep the logic and behavior of the game as accurate as possible while updating the code to compile and run on modern C compilers and operating systems.
brief.how_it_works: The C code was generated from the f77 version with f2c, the FORTRAN-to-C translator, and then modified to remove the FORTRAN I/O library, add simple more processing, and change the format of the database file. The lineage runs from MDL (MUDDLE) at MIT, to DEC FORTRAN for the PDP-11 by Bob Supnik, to f77 on UNIX, and then to C. The README also notes that Dungeon differs from Zork I, which is a microcomputer adaptation covering about a third of the original map and puzzles.

commands_seen.context: Installs the package on Fedora Linux from the official repositories, per the README's Fedora section.
Builds the game from the source files in the repository, per the README's Building from Source section.

brief.install_notes: On Fedora, the package is in the official repositories. From source, run make in the repository. The README gives no further requirements such as a compiler version, runtime, or configuration. No first-run steps are documented in the fetched text.
brief.standout: It is a faithful, machine-translated descendant of the original MIT game, with a documented chain of translations from MDL to FORTRAN to f77 to C. The README also credits the people at each step, so the port reads as a piece of computing history you can play.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README. It lists three current maintainers and describes the modern maintenance period as running from 2013-12 to present, and the Fedora packaging is mentioned. I did not see a last release date or last commit date in the fetched content, so I cannot confirm recent activity beyond that.
brief.caveats: The README describes this as a preservation project, so it aims to keep the original behavior rather than add features. The fetched text does not mention a license beyond the public-domain claim, and it does not describe platforms beyond Fedora, make builds, and the MS-DOS and Microsoft C port mentioned in the history section. Dungeon is not the same game as Zork I, which the README stresses.
